title: Agent identity/prompt is sourced from 4+ unreconciled mechanisms, and the skill.md persona pipeline is dead

deepdive.real_abstraction_trying_to_exist: A single PromptResolver / AgentPersona seam: one function `resolve_system_prompt(identity)` with a documented precedence chain (explicit caller prompt > holon active.txt > constitution-by-name > skill.md-by-role > ROLE_BRIEFINGS > generic) that every spawn route funnels through, with skill.md as the single source of truth for per-role personas (matching CLAUDE.md's stated registry and the MAP-Elites behavioral-diversity doctrine). Today no such seam exists; each spawn path improvises its own persona lookup and each silently drops the skill body.
deepdive.concept_appearing_in_too_many_places: The role/name -> persona-text mapping. It is materialized in FOUR independent registries — dharma_swarm/skills/*.skill.md (8 files), daemon_config.ROLE_BRIEFINGS (5 PSMV roles), startup_crew.DEFAULT_CREW inline system_prompt strings (lines 216-252), and agent_constitution.CONSTITUTIONAL_ROSTER (6 named agents) — and is assembled by TWO unrelated builders (agent_runner._build_system_prompt at 948-967 and autonomous_agent._build_system_prompt at 1212-1232), plus a fifth on-disk source (holon_bridge.load_holon reading .agents/<name>/prompt_variants/active.txt). Same concept, six places, none reconciled.
deepdive.missing_module_boundary: There is no prompt-resolution module. `_build_system_prompt` in agent_runner.py hard-codes `ROLE_BRIEFINGS.get(config.role.value)` as the only role->persona source and never imports skills.py. The boundary that should exist — a `persona_resolver` that owns role/name->prompt precedence and is the ONE place ROLE_BRIEFINGS, SkillRegistry, the constitutional roster, and holon active.txt are reconciled — is absent, so every consumer (agent_runner, autonomous_agent, startup_crew, stage_executor, profiles) re-derives the mapping and each drops a different field.
deepdive.why_agents_get_stuck_here: Three traps. (1) `SkillRegistry` IS imported in swarm.py, startup_crew.py, stage_executor.py, intent_router.py — so grepping "SkillRegistry" gives false confidence that skills are wired; the break is that each consumer specifically discards the `.system_prompt` field (startup_crew._crew_from_skills builds crew dicts with only name/role/thread/provider/model; stage_executor._resolve_agent returns skill.description then throws it away into `_sys` at line 156). (2) There are TWO functions literally named `_build_system_prompt` in different files, so reading one never reveals the other holon-fed path. (3) ROLE_BRIEFINGS always returns plausible text, so nothing ever errors or looks broken — the pipeline is dead silently. A grepper concludes "skills are used" and moves on.
deepdive.smallest_durable_fix: Two complementary edits, both additive. (A) In agent_runner._build_system_prompt (the one seam every AgentPool.spawn funnels through), before falling back to ROLE_BRIEFINGS, consult SkillRegistry().get(config.role.value) and use skill.system_prompt when present; ROLE_BRIEFINGS demoted to fallback for roles with no skill (operator/archivist/etc. keep working). (B) One-line fix in startup_crew._crew_from_skills (lines 375-381): add "system_prompt": skill.system_prompt to the crew dict so the crew-from-skills spawn path (which already reads spec['system_prompt'] at line 419) stops dropping the body. Add a regression test asserting cartographer.skill.md's distinguishing text (the "~/.dharma_manifest.json" manifest-verification protocol, line 25) reaches the string returned by _build_system_prompt for a cartographer-role AgentConfig.
deepdive.larger_ideal_fix: Execute the archived AGENT_IDENTITY_UNIFICATION plan (docs/_archive/2026-04/AGENT_IDENTITY_UNIFICATION.md): a single persona_resolver.resolve(name, role, provider) -> str with one documented precedence chain; retire ROLE_BRIEFINGS and DEFAULT_CREW's inline system_prompt strings (migrate their content into skill.md files); fold autonomous_agent._build_system_prompt and holon active.txt into the same resolver as explicit precedence tiers rather than a parallel assembler; make skill.md the SSOT for role personas as CLAUDE.md already claims. Extend AgentRole (or drop the enum constraint on skill-derived roles) so builder/jagat_kalyan personas are representable without a Pydantic reject.
deepdive.vision_alignment_note: The Transcendence Principle (CLAUDE.md) requires DIVERSITY OF COMPETENCE with decorrelated errors, measured via MAP-Elites behavioral descriptors. skill.md is the intended per-role, per-model-family persona SSOT that produces that behavioral diversity (cartographer on llama-3.3-70b/OpenRouter, jagat_kalyan on claude-code, etc.). Because the bodies are unreachable, actual spawned persona diversity collapses onto 5 stale PSMV ROLE_BRIEFINGS + a few hardcoded DEFAULT_CREW prompts, and — worse — silently DRIFTS every time someone edits a skill.md believing it takes effect. Decorrelation is the arithmetic that makes the ensemble beat the individual (E_ensemble = E_mean - E_diversity); a dead persona registry narrows the diversity term without any signal. This is also a documentation-vs-code split: CLAUDE.md lines 425-426 document skill.md as "swarm subagent role definitions, parsed by SkillRegistry" — over-specified in docs, under-wired in code.

All cited evidence verified against the repo exactly as stated:

1. dharma_swarm/agent_runner.py:948-967 — `_build_system_prompt` confirmed line-for-line. 2. dharma_swarm/startup_crew.py:371-381 — `_crew_from_skills` confirmed exactly; crew dicts contain only `name/role/thread/provider/model`, no `system_prompt` key. Traced one level further than the claim did: in `spawn_default_crew` (line ~417) `base_prompt = str(spec.get("system_prompt", "") or "").strip()` — since the skill-sourced dict never has that key, `base_prompt` is always empty string for skill-based crews, so only `MEMORY_SURVIVAL_INSTINCT` gets used, not the skill's persona text. This is corroborating evidence beyond what the claim cited.

3. dharma_swarm/fs_substrate/stage_executor.py:128-156 (claim said 128-156, actual function starts at 117 but the binding line is 156) — `_resolve_agent` returns `skill.description` (not even `system_prompt`) as the 4th tuple element, and the call site `agent_id, provider, model, _sys = _resolve_agent(...)` at line 156 binds it to `_sys`, which greps as used nowhere else in the file — confirmed discarded.

But this is a wholly separate, independently hardcoded roster (dharma_swarm/agent_constitution.py) unrelated to skills.py/SkillRegistry — it does not source from skill.md files, so it does not rescue skill.md persona bodies from being dead. This does not weaken the claim.

Checked realism of the proposed fix: AgentRole enum values (models.py) include cartographer, archeologist, surgeon, architect, validator, researcher — these match the skill.md basenames exactly, and SkillRegistry.get(name) keys by skill name. So `SkillRegistry().get(config.role.value).system_prompt` would actually resolve correctly for the roles that have skill files today, making the one-and-done fix realistic and low-risk (falls back safely via `.get()` returning None for roles without a matching skill).

No exaggeration or misrepresentation found; all line numbers, paths, and the commit hash check out exactly.

DEFAULT_CREW is built by _resolve_default_crew() (lines 140-197) and its dict entries carry no system_prompt key at all — only name/role/thread/provider/model. Lines 216-252 actually belong to _resolve_cybernetics_crew(), assigned to a separate module-level variable CYBERNETICS_CREW (line 261), a different crew entirely used for a "Cybernetics Directive" fleet, not the default startup crew. So the claim mislabels which variable/crew the inline system_prompt strings belong to.

The missing boundary is: registry (yaml, canonical, append-only) -> verifier (status = f(pinned test result, fixed_in ancestry), the only thing allowed to set 'resolved') -> renderer (.md as a generated view, never hand-edited for status). The half-built scripts/uplift_guards/mismatch_registry.py is the vestigial verifier boundary that was never given teeth (no open entries to check, no tests to run).

(3) Give the existing pre-commit guard teeth by adding the four genuinely-open entries (NEW-05/07/08/12) to docs/interface_mismatches.yaml with status=open and a real pinned test/SHA, so check_mismatch_adjacency stops being a permanent no-op and a resolved-flip requires that pin to flip. deepdive.vision_alignment_note: This is the codebase's VSM System-3 audit / System-2 coordination channel for its own interface integrity — the governance instrument meant to stop decorrelated agents from silently re-breaking each other's contracts. Per CLAUDE.md's Transcendence Principle, the value of many diverse agents comes from DECORRELATED errors; a lying shared map does the opposite — it broadcasts one identical false prior ('this is fixed') into every seat, correlating their errors. It is also the exact 'governance cost measured in diversity/quality loss' the principle warns about: heavy prose governance that yields false confidence. Fixing it is not scope creep — a governance channel that cannot tell true closure from same-day self-attestation is under-specified precisely where the vision needs it to be a hard, verifiable gate (the same lesson already applied to track-closure in 8f688e9f).

(6) The doc is 190 lines of prose with status in six locations; keeping all six coherent by hand is beyond what any single edit reliably achieves, so drift is the default outcome, not an accident.

deepdive.smallest_durable_fix: Extract ONE agent tool registry (single source of tool handlers + tool-definition schemas) plus ONE telos-gate invocation covering all side-effect tools, into a small shared module. Make both AgentRunner._complete_with_tool_loop and AutonomousAgent.wake resolve their tools and their gate from it. This is the highest-leverage single move: it immediately kills the 'a tool/gate/fix added to one path is not inherited by the other' harm (finding #1's recurrence), requires no rewrite of either loop, has a bounded blast radius, and needs no oracle/DST coverage the graph track hasn't built yet. It also forces the governance question — which track owns agent_runner.py/autonomous_agent.py — to be answered, because the extraction touches unowned surfaces.

deepdive.vision_alignment_note: This directly threatens the Transcendence Principle's necessary conditions. The principle wants DECORRELATED ERRORS from DIVERSE COMPETENT agents plus UNIFORM QUALITY AGGREGATION and LIGHT, CONSISTENT governance. What the two-engine split actually produces is decorrelated CAPABILITIES by accident: agents on the Orchestrator path get a 5-tool OpenAI-shaped loop with one gate battery, agents on the conductor/CLI path get a 14-tool Anthropic-shaped loop with a hardcoded 4-tool gate — the same agent role behaves differently depending on which dispatcher woke it. The telos-gate model is ALSO split (inline _SIDE_EFFECT_TOOLS set vs CORE_GATES) — governance is neither light-and-consistent nor uniformly enforced; it is duplicated and drifting. Consolidating to one engine with one registry and one gate is what makes the diversity INTENTIONAL (diverse prompts/models over identical, auditable machinery) and the governance uniform — the exact posture CLAUDE.md's Transcendence and VSM sections require.

verdict.counterevidence:
Core claim (two independently-evolved ReAct tool-loops with divergent tool registries) is real and well-supported by code, but several specific evidentiary details in the claim are inaccurate or overstated:

1. CONFIRMED: persistent_agent.py:3 quote is verbatim accurate: "Composes AutonomousAgent — does NOT inherit or reinvent the ReAct loop."
2. CONFIRMED: AutonomousAgent's loop is actually named `_reason_and_act` (lines 480-553), invoked from `wake()` at line 434 — not itself named `wake`, though the claim's citation of lines 491-553 and description of the loop mechanics (for turn in range(max_turns) -> _call_llm -> execute tools -> feed back -> break on end_turn) is accurate.
3. CONFIRMED: AutonomousAgent tool handler dict at lines 963-978 has exactly 14 entries including bash/message_agent/remember/recall/stigmergy_mark/stigmergy_read/ginko_signals/ginko_regime — matches claim.
4. CONFIRMED: _SIDE_EFFECT_TOOLS at line 951 is exactly {"bash", "write_file", "search_content", "message_agent"} — 4 items, matches claim.
5. CONFIRMED: AgentRunner._complete_with_tool_loop spans lines 1916-1996 (claim's line range is exact) and is an independently-written loop with its own round-based structure, _invoke_provider call, text-fallback tool-call parsing, and OpenAI tool-call message shape — genuinely divergent implementation from AutonomousAgent's Anthropic-block-shaped loop.
6. FACTUAL ERROR: the claim states AgentRunner's local tool loop registry is "read_file/write_file/edit_file/web_search/fetch_url only" (5 tools) and later says AutonomousAgent has "bash ... that AgentRunner's local loop lacks." This is wrong — _execute_local_tool (agent_runner.py:1792-1914) DOES include bash via the alias set `{"shell_exec", "bash"}` (line 1840), plus glob_files/search_files (1851) and grep_search/search_content (1859) — 8 distinct capabilities, not 5. The claim undercounts the registry and incorrectly asserts bash is exclusive to AutonomousAgent.
7. OVERSTATED: blast_radius claims AgentRunner's tool loop "drives every Orchestrator dispatch on the main daemon hot path." In fact _complete_with_tool_loop only fires when (a) a sandbox is attached, (b) the provider is NOT Claude Code/Codex and supports OpenAI-style tool calling (_provider_supports_local_tool_loop), and (c) the task is classified as requiring tooling (_requires_tooling) — see agent_runner.py:2020-2027. Tasks on Claude Code/Codex providers, or not requiring tooling, skip this loop entirely and go straight to _invoke_provider. This is a conditional fallback path for a specific provider subset, not a universal hot-path loop.
8. OVERSTATED/IMPRECISE ON GATES: the claim frames AutonomousAgent's `check_action` (4-tool gate) and AgentRunner's "CORE_GATES" as two different gate implementations ("the same governance concept enforced two different ways"). In fact both ultimately call the identical `TelosGatekeeper.check()` method running the same 11 CORE_GATES (telos_gates.py:408-...; check_action at :809 calls DEFAULT_GATEKEEPER.check(); agent_runner.py:2163 calls check_with_reflective_reroute, which also wraps the same TelosGatekeeper). The real, more precise (and actually more concerning) divergence is invocation granularity/scope: agent_runner gates once per whole task (task.title/description, before execution starts) while autonomous_agent gates per individual tool call for only 4 named tools — and inside AgentRunner's own _execute_local_tool loop body there is no per-tool-call gate check at all (bash calls inside the round loop are ungated after the single task-level check passes). The claim's framing of "split telos enforcement" as two different gate batteries is inaccurate; the real issue is unequal invocation scope of the same gate class.

Net: the duplication finding itself is real, verifiable, and matches a genuine architectural drift risk (new tools/gates added to one engine won't propagate to the other). But roughly a third of the specific evidence cited (tool-set enumeration, bash exclusivity, "every dispatch" blast radius claim, and the telos-gate framing) is either wrong or overstated, which should lower confidence in the claim as precisely stated even though its central thesis survives.
verdict.notes: The proposed one_and_done_fix (extract one shared tool registry + one shared gate invocation point that both engines call) is directionally reasonable and low-risk as stated, though it undersells the real complication: AgentRunner's loop uses OpenAI tool_calls message shape while AutonomousAgent uses Anthropic tool_use blocks, so "just share a registry" still requires an adapter layer per the fix's own second paragraph — that part of the fix write-up is realistic and appropriately scoped. The larger "AgentExecutionEngine" unification is correctly flagged as the bigger, riskier lift and not claimed as one_and_done.

deepdive.real_abstraction_trying_to_exist: ACTIVE_TRACK.yaml is a mutable state document with an implicit lifecycle state machine (a track id is ACTIVE xor terminal-closed; `closed_tracks` is append-only; `closed` is terminal and irreversible without an explicit reopen protocol). Today those semantics live only as prose in the file header ("Close a track by moving its block to closed_tracks (append-only)", line ~46) and are never enforced. check_track_status.py is a SNAPSHOT validator — it proves the head tree is internally well-formed — but the real missing thing is a TRANSITION validator that diffs head against the merge base and enforces the lifecycle invariants across a merge. The other latent abstraction is an external-blocker registry: a first-class ops-item node (e.g. OPS-VPS-001) that many tracks can reference via `blocked_by:` instead of each restating the same human action in prose.
deepdive.concept_appearing_in_too_many_places: "Provision the always-on daemon VPS/host" — one human ops action — is restated near-verbatim as a local next-item in three active tracks (ACTIVE_TRACK.yaml:761 and :773 organism-rewire; :397 loop-closure; :919 dharmagraph). organism-rewire even cross-references its own "VPS item 4" from another of its next-items, showing the tracks already feel the need for a shared referent but only invented it track-locally. deepdive.missing_module_boundary: Two boundaries are missing. (1) A transition/diff validator distinct from the snapshot validator: check_track_status.py builds `known_ids` as a silent UNION of active+closed ids (check_track_status.py:1542-1546), so a resurrected id is indistinguishable from a legitimate one; nowhere does it load the base ACTIVE_TRACK.yaml (no `git diff`/`git show origin/main` against the file anywhere in the script) to assert append-only closed_tracks or no active∩closed overlap. deepdive.vision_alignment_note: This is a governance-cost problem in VSM terms, not a Transcendence-Principle (diversity/decorrelation) problem. CLAUDE.md's contract is "make onboard is the only command you need to remember" and "trust the onboarding output" — i.e. ACTIVE_TRACK.yaml is the single coordination surface every agent is told to trust over its own priors. A surface that can silently show a SHIPPED track as ACTIVE for ~24 days (and survive a re-verification pass) directly corrodes that trust contract: agents burn decorrelated effort re-describing already-shipped or already-pending work (the 3x VPS restatement is the visible symptom).
